execution_batches.description: Make the consumer Lambda pure business execution and align its contract with the state machine-owned persistence model.
Refactor the Step Functions definition to preserve input context, own final persistence, and apply the new retry/failure strategy.
Validate the refactored machine locally and through manual AWS executions.

tasks.title: Remove results-table persistence from the consumer use case
outputs: Consumer Lambda returns business success data and throws classified errors without writing to tapi-results
exit_criteria: ProcessProviderRecordUseCase no longer saves success results.
ProcessProviderRecordUseCase no longer saves terminal failures.
Consumer still returns structured success payloads and throws TransientApiError or TerminalApiError as before.

tasks.title: Align consumer tests and DI with pure business execution
outputs: Consumer-side tests that validate pure provider execution and error classification only
exit_criteria: Tests no longer expect the consumer to persist success or failure results.
Consumer handler and dependency wiring remain compatible with Step Functions invocation.

tasks.title: Refactor InvokeConsumerLambda to preserve root workflow input
outputs: A Lambda invoke task that keeps recordId/providerId/scheduledDate/workflow metadata available after invocation
exit_criteria: The Lambda invoke task injects only the business payload required by tapi-consumer.
The original workflow input is still available to downstream states after InvokeConsumerLambda.
The Lambda success result is stored under a dedicated result node rather than replacing the root input.

tasks.title: Move final success and failure persistence into native DynamoDB task states
outputs: State-machine-owned success and failure persistence paths
exit_criteria: Success path writes to tapi-results using native DynamoDB integration.
Terminal failure path writes to tapi-results using native DynamoDB integration.
Exhausted transient failure path writes to tapi-results using native DynamoDB integration.
Duplicate executions remain a no-op and do not write to tapi-results.

tasks.title: Finalize retry, catch, and lifecycle closure semantics in the state machine
outputs: A corrected state machine definition aligned with the phase-2 state-machine spec
exit_criteria: Retry block covers transient provider failures with BackoffRate 2.0 and JitterStrategy FULL.
Terminal failures are routed directly to the failure path without retry.
Exhausted transient retries also route to the failure path.
Success path marks idempotency COMPLETED and pending record COMPLETED.
Failure path marks idempotency FAILED and pending record FAILED.

tasks.title: Validate local build, tests, and CDK synthesis for the refactored workflow
outputs: Passing local quality gates for the refactored state machine
exit_criteria: npm run build passes.
npm test -- --runInBand passes with updated expectations.
npx cdk synth TapiStack succeeds with the new state-machine definition.

tasks.title: Validate manual AWS execution paths for success, terminal failure, transient retry, and duplicate no-op
outputs: Operational proof that the state machine now owns persistence and lifecycle closure correctly
exit_criteria: A valid pending record on HTTP 200 reaches success persistence and pending COMPLETED.
A valid pending record on HTTP 400 reaches failure persistence and pending FAILED without retry.
A valid pending record on HTTP 503 retries with jittered backoff and reaches exhausted failure if attempts are consumed.
A duplicate or already-claimed record ends in DuplicateWorkItem without invoking the consumer or writing to tapi-results.
